html:
Cnut the Great was a Danish prince who became king of England in 1016, of Denmark in 1018 and of Norway in 1028. He ruled an empire around the North Sea until he died in 1035.

He was the son of Sweyn Forkbeard, who had conquered England just before his death. Cnut won it back after hard fighting and married Emma, the widow of the English king. He ruled England mostly through English nobles and the church, and went on pilgrimage to Rome in 1027 for the crowning of the emperor.

His empire did not outlast his sons. But his reign marked the end of the raiding Viking Age and the arrival of Denmark among the Christian kingdoms of Europe, a path begun by his grandfather Harald Bluetooth at Jelling.
sum: Cnut the Great was a Danish prince who became king of England in 1016, of Denmark in 1018 and of Norway in 1028. He ruled an empire around the North Sea until he died in 1035.
